findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 1479 of 2128 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A small file for most flat-fare systems.
findings.fix: Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
findings.what: The feed contains no fare information.
findings.why: Riders see 'fare unknown' in trip planners and can't budget their trip; visitors are most affected.

findings.effort: One field.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 30% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (26% marked accessible, 4% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is not published.

findings.effort: Usually one export setting.
findings.fix: Turn on shape cleanup in your export tool, or drop the repeated points from shapes.txt.
findings.what: Some route lines list the same point twice in a row.
findings.why: Repeated points don't hurt riders, but they can skew distance math and hint at a shaky export.

findings.effort: Usually an export-tool fix, not hand editing.
findings.fix: Re-generate shape_dist_traveled on export so stop and shape distances use the same units.
findings.what: On some trips the stop distances run a little past the end of the route line.
findings.why: The stop and shape distance values don't quite line up, so any math that uses them can drift.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'equal_shape_distance_diff_coordinates_distance_below_threshold' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Equal shape distance diff coordinates distance below threshold (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A few minutes in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Delete the empty calendars or set their service days.
findings.what: Some service calendars have no days of the week switched on.
findings.why: Trips tied to these calendars never run; they are dead data that can mask real schedule problems.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stop times for transposed minutes.
findings.what: Some scheduled trips move faster between stops than a transit vehicle can.
findings.why: Usually a typo'd stop time; riders get arrival times no transit vehicle can meet.

findings.effort: One setting in most export tools.
findings.fix: Remove past service periods the next time you export the feed.
findings.what: Some service calendars in the feed have already ended.
findings.why: Expired calendars are dead weight and can hide real schedule problems from your staff and vendors.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'route_short_name_too_long' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Route short name too long (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Usually an export-tool fix, not hand editing.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stops' shape_dist_traveled against the route shape, and re-generate it on export if they disagree.
findings.what: Some stops sit far from the route line, going by the feed's own distance values.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the route down the wrong path or point riders to the wrong boarding location.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the stop order and the shape direction in your scheduling software; the shape is often drawn backwards.
findings.what: On some trips the stops fall along the route line in a different order than the schedule lists.
findings.why: Trip planners can draw the transit vehicle doubling back or skipping ahead, which confuses riders reading the map.

findings.effort: Usually one export setting.
findings.fix: Trim leading and trailing spaces on export. The scorecard's auto-fixed copy already does this.
findings.what: Some values have extra spaces at the start or end.
findings.why: A stray space can break a match, so a stop or route may fail to link across files.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: One field per route.
findings.fix: Pick a darker/lighter route_text_color for the flagged routes.
findings.what: Some route colors don't contrast with their text color.
findings.why: Route badges get hard to read, most of all for riders with low vision.

findings.effort: Usually a bulk edit in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Set trip_headsign to the trip's last stop or its overall destination.
findings.what: Some trip headsigns name a stop along the way, not the final destination.
findings.why: The sign should tell riders where the transit vehicle ends up, so a midpoint name can send them the wrong way.

findings.effort: Two fields in feed_info.txt, or one export setting.
findings.fix: Widen feed_start_date and feed_end_date to cover all service dates, or fix the dates that fall outside.
findings.what: Some service dates fall outside the date window set in feed_info.txt.
findings.why: feed_info.txt should span every day your service runs, so apps know when the data applies.

findings.effort: A review of your calendar dates.
findings.fix: Check whether the gap is real, like a seasonal break; if not, add the missing dates to the calendar.
findings.what: The feed has a stretch of two weeks or more with no service running.
findings.why: A long gap can mean dates were left out of the calendar. Apps then show no trips on those days.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'unsorted_stop_times' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Unsorted stop times (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged files.
findings.fix: Check the flagged column names for misspellings of standard GTFS fields; remove them if they are vendor extras.
findings.what: Some files contain columns that are not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Harmless to riders, but apps ignore these columns and they can hide typos in real column names.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 89 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (FIL 2, FIL 3, FIL B1, FIL B4, FIL 10, and more).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 3 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("Colbert / CFA", "Colbert / CFA", "Camping Terre & Mer").
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.
